concepts.name: Parliament, the Rajya Sabha and its composition
concepts.description: Article 79 and the role of Parliament, bicameralism, the Provisional Parliament, Article 80 composition of the Rajya Sabha, its election, qualifications, duration and Chairman.
concepts.idea: Parliament is the President plus two Houses; the Rajya Sabha is a permanent House of at most 250 members, indirectly elected by STV with 12 nominees, chaired ex officio by the Vice-President.
concepts.rule: Article 79 makes Parliament the President, the Council of States and the House of the People; it controls the executive (Art 75), amends the Constitution (Art 368) and approves taxes and spending. The Constituent Assembly acted as the Provisional Parliament from 1950 to 1951-52 (Art 379). The Rajya Sabha has at most 250 members (238 from States and UTs, 12 nominated); Laxmikanth gives 245 now (225 States, 8 UTs, 12 nominated), with only Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir represented among UTs. State members are elected by the elected Assembly members by STV. Since 2003 a candidate need be an elector only in some parliamentary constituency. It is never dissolved, a third retires every second year and the term is six years under the RPA 1951; the Vice-President is ex officio Chairman (Art 89(1)).
concepts.example: A candidate registered as an elector in Bihar may contest a Rajya Sabha seat from Kerala since the 2003 change.

questions.q: Article 79 provides for the constitution of Parliament. Which one of the following is an integral part of Parliament although he is not a member of either House?
questions.e: Article 79 makes Parliament consist of the President, the Council of States and the House of the People; the President follows the British 'Crown in Parliament' pattern and sits in neither House (also in Laxmikanth ch23 p.327).
w: The Vice-President presides over the Rajya Sabha ex officio but is not a constituent part of Parliament under Article 79.
The Prime Minister must be a member of one House, and is not a separate part of Parliament.
The Attorney General may speak in either House but is not a constituent part of Parliament.

questions.q: Article 80 fixes the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha. Which one of the following correctly states how that maximum is made up?
questions.a: 238 representatives of States and Union Territories and 12 nominated by the President
o: 238 representatives of States and Union Territories and 12 nominated by the President
233 representatives of the States and Union Territories and 12 members nominated by the President
230 representatives of the States and Union Territories and 20 members nominated by the President
250 representatives of the States and Union Territories with no member nominated at all
questions.e: The ceiling of 250 splits into 238 representatives of States and UTs and 12 nominated members (Laxmikanth ch23 p.327).
w: 233 plus 12 is the present strength of 245, not the constitutional maximum of 250.
The nominated quota is 12, not 20.
The nominated members are part of the 250; the quota is not zero.

questions.q: Ravi is registered as an elector in a parliamentary constituency in Bihar and wishes to contest a Rajya Sabha seat from Kerala. Which of the following is correct about his candidature, in the light of the change of 2003?
questions.a: He qualifies on this count, as an elector in any parliamentary constituency of India
o: He qualifies on this count, as an elector in any parliamentary constituency of India
He fails the requirement, because he must be an elector in Kerala, the State he seeks to represent in the Council of States
He fails the requirement, because the 2003 change relaxed the elector rule only for Lok Sabha candidates
He qualifies only if he has previously held a legislative office in the State of Kerala
questions.e: In 2003 the Representation of the People Act was amended so that a Rajya Sabha candidate need not be an elector of the State he represents; registration as an elector in any parliamentary constituency suffices (Laxmikanth ch23 p.332).
w: The elector-in-that-State rule was dispensed with in 2003.
The 2003 change concerned Rajya Sabha candidates; Lok Sabha candidates were never tied to a State in this way.
Prior legislative office is not a qualification for Rajya Sabha membership.

questions.q: According to Laxmikanth, which one of the following sets lists all the Union Territories that have representation in the Rajya Sabha?
questions.a: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
o: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
Delhi, Chandigarh and Jammu and Kashmir
Puducherry, Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir
questions.e: Of the eight Union Territories only Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir are represented; the rest are too small in population, and the representation is decided by Parliament by law (Laxmikanth ch23 p.328).
w: Chandigarh has no Rajya Sabha seat, and Jammu and Kashmir is omitted.
Chandigarh has no Rajya Sabha seat, and Puducherry is omitted.
Ladakh has no Rajya Sabha seat, and Delhi is omitted.

questions.q: The Vice-President of India is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article 89(1). What does 'ex officio' signify here?
questions.a: He gets the chair by holding the office of Vice-President, not by election to the House
o: He gets the chair by holding the office of Vice-President, not by election to the House
He is elected to the chair by the members of the Rajya Sabha from among themselves
He is nominated to the chair by the President for a fixed term of office
He holds the chair only until the Rajya Sabha elects a Chairman from among its members
questions.e: Ex officio means by virtue of another office: the Vice-President becomes Chairman automatically, whereas the Deputy Chairman is elected by the House (Laxmikanth ch23 p.340).
w: Election by House members from among themselves is the method for the Deputy Chairman.
The Chairman is not nominated by the President; the post comes with the vice-presidency.
The Rajya Sabha has no power to elect its own Chairman.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Parliament's control over the executive:

1. Under Article 75 the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to both Houses of Parliament equally.
2. Question Hour, Zero Hour and Half-an-Hour Discussion are among the devices through which Parliament scrutinises the executive.
3. Financial scrutiny is done by the Public Accounts Committee, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings.
4. No tax can be levied and no expenditure incurred without parliamentary approval.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 75 makes it collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha alone. Statement 2 is correct: They are listed as control devices. Statement 3 is correct: These are the three financial committees. Statement 4 is correct: The budget process under Articles 112-114 embodies this.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.81
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.81
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.81

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the amending power of Parliament:

1. Article 368 gives Parliament power to amend the Constitution by addition, variation or repeal.
2. Most provisions need a majority of the total membership of each House and two-thirds of the members present and voting.
3. The formation of a new State under Articles 2 to 4 requires a special majority under Article 368.
4. Federal provisions need the special majority plus ratification by at least half of the State legislatures.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: This is the constituent power. Statement 2 is correct: This is the special majority. Statement 3 is incorrect: Such changes are made by ordinary law, outside Article 368 (Laxmikanth ch11 p.194). Statement 4 is correct: This is the third route (Laxmikanth ch11 p.194).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.81
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.81
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.81

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers of Parliament:

1. The initiative to amend the Constitution lies with Parliament and not with the States.
2. The procedure for impeaching the President in Article 61 applies equally to the removal of the Vice-President.
3. Parliament can impeach the President for violating the Constitution.
4. Parliament can punish both its members and outsiders for breach of privilege or contempt of the House.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A State legislature can only ask Parliament by resolution in limited cases. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Vice-President is removed under Article 67 by a resolution that must originate in the Rajya Sabha (Laxmikanth ch19 p.304). Statement 3 is correct: Article 61. Statement 4 is correct: Parliament can punish both its members and outsiders for breach of privilege or contempt of the House.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.81
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.81
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.81

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Provisional Parliament:

1. The Constituent Assembly functioned as the Provisional Parliament from 1950 until the first general elections of 1951-52.
2. Laws made by it had the status of constitutional provisions.
3. G.V. Mavalankar was Speaker of the Constituent Assembly (Legislative) as well as of the Provisional Parliament.
4. It was a bicameral body made up of a Council of States and a House of the People.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 379 (Laxmikanth ch2 p.42). Statement 2 is incorrect: They were ordinary laws. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.339. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Provisional Parliament was the single-chamber Constituent Assembly itself; the two Houses came with the first elected Parliament (Laxmikanth ch2 p.42).
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.81
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.81
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.81

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the bicameral structure of Parliament:

1. Parliament must have two Houses, whereas a State may have either one or two.
2. The Lok Sabha is the House of the States, while the Rajya Sabha speaks for the people of India at large.
3. Bicameralism is meant mainly to speed up legislation by avoiding revision and reconsideration of Bills.
4. Article 80 provides that the Rajya Sabha represents the States and not the Union Territories.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 79 and. Statement 2 is incorrect: The reverse is true (Laxmikanth ch23 p.327). Statement 3 is incorrect: The second House provides revision and protection against hasty law-making. Statement 4 is incorrect: It represents the States and Union Territories.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.81
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.81
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.81

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Rajya Sabha:

1. According to Laxmikanth, the present strength is 245, of whom 225 represent States, 8 represent Union Territories and 12 are nominated.
2. Persons of eminence in literature, science, art and social service can enter the Rajya Sabha by presidential nomination, without an election.
3. Seats are allotted broadly on population, so Uttar Pradesh has 31 members and Tripura has one.
4. The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats among the States and Union Territories.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.327. Statement 2 is correct: Persons of eminence in literature, science, art and social service can enter the Rajya Sabha by presidential nomination, without an election. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.328. Statement 4 is correct: The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats among the States and Union Territories.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.327
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.327
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.327

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the election of Rajya Sabha members:

1. Members of the State Legislative Councils also vote in the election of the State's Rajya Sabha members.
2. The election of State representatives is by proportional representation with the single transferable vote.
3. Representatives of a Union Territory are chosen by an electoral college constituted for the purpose.
4. The representation of a Union Territory in the Rajya Sabha is not automatic but decided by Parliament by law.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Only the elected members of the Legislative Assembly vote (Laxmikanth ch23 p.328). Statement 2 is correct: The election of State representatives is by proportional representation with the single transferable vote. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.328. Statement 4 is correct: The representation of a Union Territory in the Rajya Sabha is not automatic but decided by Parliament by law.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.82
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.82
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.82

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about qualifications for the Rajya Sabha:

1. Article 84 requires a member to be a citizen of India and at least 30 years of age.
2. Not holding an office of profit is one of the qualifications listed in Article 84.
3. Parliament has required by law that a candidate be registered as an elector in a parliamentary constituency.
4. Article 84 lays down the positive qualifications, while Article 102 lists the disqualifications.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 84 requires a member to be a citizen of India and at least 30 years of age. Statement 2 is incorrect: Office of profit is a disqualification under Article 102(1)(a), not an Article 84 qualification (loosely; Laxmikanth ch23 p.332). Statement 3 is correct: Representation of the People Act 1951 (Laxmikanth ch23 p.332). Statement 4 is correct: Article 84 lays down the positive qualifications, while Article 102 lists the disqualifications.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.82
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.82
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.82

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the duration of the Rajya Sabha:

1. It is a continuing House that is not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every second year.
2. The term of a member is six years, fixed by the Representation of the People Act 1951.
3. The Chairman of the House is elected by its members from among themselves.
4. Retiring members are eligible for re-election any number of times.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.331. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.331. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Vice-President is Chairman ex officio (Article 89(1)); only the Deputy Chairman is elected. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.331.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.82
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.82
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.82

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha:

1. Its present strength is 250, of whom 233 are elected and 12 are nominated.
2. Five Union Territories have no seat, because Laxmikanth treats their populations as too small.
3. The nominated members are elected by the members of the State Legislative Assemblies.
4. As in the United States Senate, each State gets an equal number of seats.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: 233 plus 12 makes 245; 250 is the maximum. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.328. Statement 3 is incorrect: They are nominated by the President. Statement 4 is incorrect: Seats vary with population, unlike the Senate (Laxmikanth ch23 p.328). So exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Calling Attention Motion and the No-Confidence Motion are devices of parliamentary control over the executive.
2. Parliament sets in motion the removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges, the CAG and the Chief Election Commissioner.
3. The financial scrutiny committees are the Public Accounts Committee, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Subordinate Legislation.
4. Parliament can impeach the President for violation of the Constitution under Article 61.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Calling Attention Motion and the No-Confidence Motion are devices of parliamentary control over the executive. Statement 2 is correct: Parliament sets in motion the removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges, the CAG and the Chief Election Commissioner. Statement 3 is incorrect: The third financial committee is the Committee on Public Undertakings, not Subordinate Legislation. Statement 4 is correct: Article 61 (Laxmikanth ch19). So exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. A State legislature cannot itself initiate an amendment Bill; the initiative lies with Parliament.
2. A special majority under Article 368 means two-thirds of the total membership of each House.
3. A change in the salaries of Members of Parliament needs a special majority under Article 368.
4. Article 368 allows Parliament to amend the Constitution by addition, variation or repeal.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A State legislature cannot itself initiate an amendment Bill; the initiative lies with Parliament. Statement 2 is incorrect: A special majority is a majority of the total membership of each House plus two-thirds of the members present and voting (Laxmikanth ch11 p.194). Statement 3 is incorrect: They lie outside Article 368 and are fixed by ordinary law (Laxmikanth ch11 p.194). Statement 4 is correct: . So exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Rajya Sabha, unlike the Lok Sabha, is not subject to dissolution.
Statement-II: A member of the Rajya Sabha must be at least thirty years of age, whereas a member of the Lok Sabha must be at least twenty-five.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Rajya Sabha is a continuing House (Laxmikanth ch23 p.331). Statement-II is correct: the minimum age is 30 for the Rajya Sabha and 25 for the Lok Sabha (Article 84). The age limit has no bearing on why the House is not dissolved, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.
w: The age qualification is a different matter from the House's continuity, so it cannot be the reason.
Statement-II is not incorrect: Article 84 fixes 30 for the Rajya Sabha and 25 for the Lok Sabha.
Statement-I is not incorrect: the Rajya Sabha is never dissolved.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A defeat of the Government on a vote in the Rajya Sabha does not oblige the Council of Ministers to resign.
Statement-II: Under Article 75 the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the ministry survives a defeat in the Rajya Sabha. Statement-II is correct: Article 75(3) makes the Council collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha alone. Because accountability runs to the Lok Sabha only, a loss in the Rajya Sabha does not force resignation; Statement-II explains Statement-I.
w: Statement-II gives the very reason Statement-I holds, so it does explain it.
Statement-II is not incorrect: Article 75 fixes responsibility to the Lok Sabha.
Statement-I is not incorrect: the Rajya Sabha cannot unseat the Government.
tr: collective responsibility is to one House

questions.q:
Match the entries in List-I with the correct entries in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 79
B. Article 80
C. Article 84
D. Article 89

List-II
1. Composition of the Council of States
2. Qualifications for membership of Parliament
3. Constitution of Parliament
4. Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States
questions.e: Article 79 constitutes Parliament; Article 80 deals with the Council of States' composition; Article 84 with qualifications; Article 89 with the Chairman and Deputy Chairman.
w: A and B are interchanged: Article 79 constitutes Parliament and Article 80 gives the Rajya Sabha's composition.
B and C are interchanged: Article 84 sets qualifications.
C and D are interchanged: Article 89 is about the presiding officers.

concepts.name: Rajya Sabha presiding officers, Lok Sabha composition and qualifications
concepts.description: The Deputy Chairman and the panel of Vice-Chairpersons, Articles 90-92, the 550 and 543 strength of the Lok Sabha, the Anglo-Indian nomination, seat allotment and Article 84 qualifications.
concepts.idea: The Rajya Sabha chair is filled in layers (Chairman, Deputy Chairman, panel, House's choice), while the Lok Sabha has a ceiling of 550 and members must meet Article 84.
concepts.rule: The Deputy Chairman is elected by the House, resigns to the Chairman and is removed under Article 90 by a majority of all then members after 14 days' notice; Article 91 lets him act for the Chairman, and Article 92 bars the Vice-President from presiding on his own removal resolution, though he may speak without voting. The panel of Vice-Chairpersons is nominated under the House rules. The Lok Sabha maximum is 550 (530 States, 20 UTs) and the present strength 543 (524 and 19). The Anglo-Indian nomination ended on 25 January 2020 (104th Amendment, after the 95th had extended it to 2020). Seats are allotted by population ratio (not for States below six million). Article 84 requires citizenship, an oath before a person authorised by the Election Commission and age 30 (Rajya Sabha) or 25 (Lok Sabha).
concepts.example: If both the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman offices are vacant, a member appointed by the President acts and the panel cannot preside.

questions.q: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha holds office while he remains a member of the House. Which one of the following states how he may be removed?
questions.a: By a resolution of a majority of all the then members, moved after 14 days' notice
o: By a resolution of a majority of all the then members, moved after 14 days' notice
By a resolution of two-thirds of the members present and voting, moved after 14 days' notice
By a resolution of a majority of the members present and voting, moved after seven days' notice
By a resolution of the Rajya Sabha that the Lok Sabha also agrees to, moved after 14 days' notice
questions.e: Article 90 lets the House remove its Deputy Chairman by a resolution of an effective majority (all then members) with 14 days' prior notice; he resigns by writing to the Chairman (Laxmikanth ch23 p.341).
w: Two-thirds of those present and voting is a special majority, not asked for here.
A simple majority and a seven-day notice are both wrong.
The Lok Sabha plays no part in removing the Deputy Chairman; that is a feature of Vice-President's removal.

questions.q: A panel of Vice-Chairpersons exists to preside over the Rajya Sabha in the absence of the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman. By whom, and under what, is the panel nominated?
questions.a: By the Chairman, under the Rules of the Rajya Sabha
o: By the Chairman, under the Rules of the Rajya Sabha
By the President, under Article 91 of the Constitution
By the Deputy Chairman, under Article 89 of the Constitution
By the House itself through election, under Article 90 of the Constitution
questions.e: The Chairman nominates the panel from among the members under the House's rules; it is a procedural device and not a constitutional office (Laxmikanth ch23 p.341).
w: Article 91 only lets the House decide who presides if the rules do not; the President does not nominate the panel.
The Deputy Chairman does not nominate the panel and Article 89 is about the Chairman and Deputy Chairman.
The panel is not elected and Article 90 concerns the Deputy Chairman's vacating of office.

questions.q: After the 104th Amendment Act, 2019, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 550. Which one of the following gives its make-up?
questions.a: 530 members from the States and 20 from the Union Territories
o: 530 members from the States and 20 from the Union Territories
524 members from the States and 19 from the Union Territories
520 members from the States and 30 from the Union Territories
545 members from the States and 5 from the Union Territories
questions.e: The ceiling of 550 consists of 530 State members and 20 Union Territory members; the present strength of 543 is 524 plus 19 (Laxmikanth ch23 p.328).
w: 524 and 19 add up to the present strength of 543, not the ceiling.
The Constitution allows 20, not 30, Union Territory seats.
The Union Territory quota is 20, not 5.

questions.q: How are the members of the Lok Sabha who represent the States chosen?
questions.a: By direct election by voters on the basis of universal adult suffrage
o: By direct election by voters on the basis of universal adult suffrage
By indirect election by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
By direct election by voters through the single transferable vote in multi-member constituencies
By nomination of the President on the advice of the Election Commission of India
questions.e: Lok Sabha members from the States are chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies on universal adult suffrage (Articles 79 and 81; also in Laxmikanth ch23 p.328). Indirect election by assemblies is the method for Rajya Sabha members from the States.
w: Indirect election by the Assembly members is the Rajya Sabha method, not the Lok Sabha method.
Lok Sabha members are elected one per territorial constituency; the single transferable vote is used for the Rajya Sabha and Presidential elections.
The President nominates no Lok Sabha members from the States; the Anglo-Indian nomination, now ended, was only for two seats.

questions.q: Members of the Lok Sabha from the Union Territories are chosen by direct election. Which one of the following provides for this?
questions.a: The Union Territories (Direct Election to the House of the People) Act, 1965
o: The Union Territories (Direct Election to the House of the People) Act, 1965
The Representation of the People Act, 1950, which allots seats and prepares electoral rolls
The Government of Union Territories Act, 1963, which gave territories their legislatures
The Delimitation Commission Act, 2002, which readjusts constituencies after a census
questions.e: The Constitution lets Parliament prescribe how UT members are chosen, and the 1965 Act provides direct election (Laxmikanth ch23 p.328).
w: The 1950 Act deals with allotment of seats and electoral rolls, not with how Union Territory members are chosen.
The 1963 Act creates legislatures and councils of ministers for Union Territories, not Lok Sabha elections.
The 2002 Act governs readjustment of constituencies.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:

1. He is elected by the members of the Rajya Sabha from among themselves.
2. He resigns by writing to the President.
3. His removal needs a resolution of a majority of all then members, moved after 14 days' notice.
4. He performs the Chairman's duties when that office is vacant or when the Vice-President is acting as President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 89. Statement 2 is incorrect: He resigns by writing to the Chairman (Laxmikanth ch23 p.341). Statement 3 is correct: Article 90. Statement 4 is correct: Article 91.

concepts.name: Delimitation, electoral systems, disqualification and vacation of seats
concepts.description: Delimitation Commission Acts and freezes, FPTP versus PR, Article 102 disqualifications, Article 101 vacation of seats, Articles 103-106 and pay.
concepts.idea: Membership of Parliament is lost or barred by disqualification (Art 102), vacation (Art 101), and decided by the President on the Election Commission's opinion (Art 103).
concepts.rule: Delimitation Commission Acts were passed in 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002; the 42nd Amendment froze seat allocation at the 1971 level and the 84th Amendment extended it to 2026. FPTP uses single-member constituencies and a plurality; PR allots seats by vote share. Article 102(1) gives five grounds: office of profit, unsound mind, undischarged insolvent, citizenship and law of Parliament. Double membership, resignation (33rd Amendment 1974), 60 days' absence, void election, expulsion and appointment as Governor vacate the seat. Article 103: President on the Election Commission's opinion. Article 104: Rs 500 per day. Article 106 fixes pay; Article 97 officers' pay; the 1953 Act.
concepts.example: Elected to Parliament and to a State legislature, a person must resign the State seat within 14 days or his parliamentary seat falls vacant.

questions.q: Parliament has enacted Delimitation Commission Acts to readjust Lok Sabha constituencies after censuses. In which years were these Acts passed?
questions.e: Laxmikanth lists the Delimitation Commission Acts of 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002 (Laxmikanth ch23 p.329).
w: The census years 1951-2001 are not the years of the Acts.
There was no Act in 1982; the freeze on readjustment began with the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
The Acts of 1950 and 1960 do not exist in this series.

questions.q: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 froze the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among the States at the 1971 level. According to Laxmikanth, the 84th Amendment Act, 2001 extended this ban on readjustment, with the same objective of encouraging population limiting measures, up to which year?
questions.e: The ban was extended by 25 years to 2026 by the 84th Amendment (Laxmikanth ch23 p.329).
w: 2031 would be a 30-year extension.
2021 would be a 20-year extension.
2051 is not the end of the extension.

questions.q: Under Article 101(3) of the Constitution, a member of Parliament who wishes to resign his seat addresses his resignation to whom?

The Secretary-General of the House to which the member belongs
The Prime Minister, as the leader of the House in which he sits

w: The President takes no part in a member's resignation; the presiding officer of the House does.
The Secretary-General is an official of the House and has no power to accept a resignation.

questions.q: A person who sits or votes in a House before taking the oath, or while knowing that he is disqualified, incurs a penalty under Article 104. What is the penalty?

o: A fine of Rs 500 for each day he sits or votes

Disqualification from membership of Parliament for six years
Suspension from the House for the remainder of the session
questions.e: Article 104 imposes a financial penalty of Rs 500 per day (Laxmikanth ch23 p.335); it is not a disqualification.

Suspension is a disciplinary power of the House, unrelated to Article 104.

questions.q: A House of Parliament may declare vacant the seat of a member who is absent from all its meetings without permission. After how many days of absence, and with what exclusion in counting, may it do so?

'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about disqualification grounds under Article 102(1):

1. The office-of-profit ground has no exception, because even a Minister is disqualified for holding an office of profit.
2. A person is disqualified if declared of unsound mind by any hospital or medical authority.
3. Ceasing to be a citizen, voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship or acknowledging allegiance to a foreign state is a ground.
4. An undischarged insolvent is disqualified.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Parliament may exempt offices, and Laxmikanth also excludes the office of Minister. Statement 2 is incorrect: The declaration must be by a competent court. Statement 3 is correct: Ceasing to be a citizen, voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship or acknowledging allegiance to a foreign state is a ground. Statement 4 is correct: . So exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. A seat that falls vacant on disqualification under Article 102 or the Tenth Schedule is a consequence of the disqualification, not a punishment.
2. The presiding officer may refuse to accept a resignation if he is satisfied that it is not voluntary or genuine.
3. Article 102 lays down when a member's seat becomes vacant.
4. Offices such as that of Governor are incompatible with membership and vacate the parliamentary seat.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A seat that falls vacant on disqualification under Article 102 or the Tenth Schedule is a consequence of the disqualification, not a punishment. Statement 2 is correct: the 33rd Amendment Act 1974 inserted this in Article 101(3)(b) (Laxmikanth ch23 p.334). Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 101 deals with vacation of seats; Article 102 lists disqualifications. Statement 4 is correct: . So exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about electoral systems and delimitation:

1. The first-past-the-post system makes a party's seats proportional to its share of votes.
2. Examples of first-past-the-post are the United Kingdom and India; Israel and the Netherlands use proportional representation.
3. Seats were reallocated among States after the 1991 census.
4. Before 2019 the Lok Sabha seats of Jammu and Kashmir were delimited under the J&K Constitution.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It can give a party more seats than its vote share. Statement 2 is correct: Examples of first-past-the-post are the United Kingdom and India; Israel and the Netherlands use proportional representation. Statement 3 is incorrect: No inter-state reallocation took place after the 1981, 1991 and 2001 censuses. Statement 4 is incorrect: Its Lok Sabha seats were delimited under the Indian Constitution; only Assembly seats followed the J&K Constitution. So exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A member of Parliament who voluntarily acquires the citizenship of a foreign State incurs disqualification under Article 102.
Statement-II: Indian citizenship is a basic qualification for membership of either House of Parliament, and a member who voluntarily takes another State's citizenship no longer meets it.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship is a ground in Article 102(1). Statement-II is correct: Article 84 requires a member to be a citizen of India, and a member who voluntarily takes another State's citizenship no longer meets that requirement. Statement-II therefore states the reason why Statement-I follows and explains it.
w: Statement-II states the qualification a member ceases to meet on taking foreign citizenship, so it does explain Statement-I.
Statement-II is not incorrect: Article 84 requires citizenship.
Statement-I is not incorrect: foreign citizenship voluntarily acquired is a ground under Article 102.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: An Indian elected both to Parliament and to a State legislature has a fortnight to resign the State seat.
Statement-II: If he fails to do so, his State legislature seat is vacated automatically.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: (Laxmikanth ch23 p.334). Statement-II is incorrect: if he does not resign the State seat within 14 days, it is his parliamentary seat that becomes vacant (Article 101(2)).
w: Statement-II names the wrong seat, so the pair cannot both be correct.
Statement-II is not correct, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

B. Article 102

2. Decision on disqualification questions by the President on the Election Commission's opinion

C and D are swapped: Article 103 is the decision rule and Article 106 is pay.

concepts.name: The Speaker, the Deputy Speaker and the Speaker Pro Tem
concepts.description: Articles 93-97: election, tenure, powers, resignation and removal of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker, and the Speaker Pro Tem.
concepts.idea: The Speaker is elected by the House, stays through dissolution until the new House meets, is removed only by an effective majority and votes only to break a tie.
concepts.rule: The Speaker is elected by a simple majority; the President fixes the date, while the Speaker fixes that of the Deputy Speaker. Removal needs a resolution of a majority of all then members after 14 days' notice (Art 94); he cannot preside then but may vote in the first instance. He resigns to the Deputy Speaker, maintains order, interprets the Rules, presides over joint sittings, certifies Money Bills and decides Tenth Schedule cases (reviewable: Kihoto Hollohan 1992). The Deputy Speaker has only a casting vote while presiding and chairs any committee he joins. After a general election the President appoints a Speaker Pro Tem (senior-most member) who swears in members and enables the election of the Speaker.
concepts.example: On dissolution the Speaker stays until the new House meets, hence a Pro Tem Speaker presides at its first sitting.

questions.q: The election of the Speaker and of the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha requires a date to be fixed. Who fixes each date?
questions.a: The President fixes the date for the Speaker and the Speaker fixes the date for the Deputy Speaker
o: The President fixes the date for the Speaker and the Speaker fixes the date for the Deputy Speaker
The President fixes the date for both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker
The Speaker fixes the date for himself and the President fixes the date for the Deputy Speaker
The Prime Minister fixes the date for the Speaker and the Speaker fixes the date for the Deputy Speaker
questions.e: The President fixes the date of the Speaker's election; the Speaker fixes that of the Deputy Speaker (Laxmikanth ch23 pp.336, 338).
w: The Deputy Speaker's date is fixed by the Speaker, not the President.
The Speaker cannot fix the date of his own election, and the President does not fix the Deputy Speaker's.
The Prime Minister has no such role.

questions.q: Under Article 94 the Speaker of the Lok Sabha can be removed from office. Which one of the following describes the procedure correctly?
questions.a: A resolution passed by a majority of all the then members, moved after 14 days' notice
o: A resolution passed by a majority of all the then members, moved after 14 days' notice
A resolution passed by two-thirds of the members present and voting, moved after 14 days' notice
A resolution passed by a majority of the members present and voting, moved on a day's notice
A resolution passed in a joint sitting of both Houses by a majority of the members present and voting
questions.e: Removal needs an effective majority (all then members) and 14 days' notice (Laxmikanth ch23 p.336).
w: Two-thirds of those present and voting is a special majority, which the Constitution does not ask here.
A simple majority on short notice does not meet Article 94.
No joint sitting is involved; the Lok Sabha alone acts.

questions.q: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha resigns from his office under Article 94 by writing to whom?
o: The Prime Minister, as Leader of the House
questions.e: The resignation letter is addressed to the Deputy Speaker (Laxmikanth ch23 p.336).
w: The Speaker is elected by the House and does not address the President.
The Prime Minister has no role in a Speaker's resignation.
The Leader of the Opposition has no role in it.

questions.q: A general election has been held and the Lok Sabha has been dissolved. In what position is the Speaker of the dissolved House?
questions.a: He remains in office until the newly elected Lok Sabha meets
o: He remains in office until the newly elected Lok Sabha meets
He vacates office on the day of dissolution and a Speaker Pro Tem takes charge
He remains in office until the new House elects its Speaker
He remains in office for six months, as the life of a House is extended in an emergency
questions.e: Unlike a Minister, the Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution; he continues until the new House meets, immediately before which he vacates (Laxmikanth ch23 pp.336, 340).
w: He does not vacate on dissolution; the Pro Tem Speaker comes in after he vacates just before the first meeting.
He vacates immediately before the first meeting, before any new Speaker is elected, and the Pro Tem presides in between.
An emergency extends the life of the House, not the Speaker's tenure after dissolution.

questions.q: The quorum for a meeting of the Lok Sabha is one-tenth of the total membership, including the presiding officer. With the present strength of 543, what is the minimum number required to transact business?
questions.e: One-tenth of 543 is 54.3, so at least 55 members must be present (Laxmikanth ch23 p.345). In the absence of quorum the Speaker adjourns or suspends the sitting.
w: 181 is one-third of 543.
109 is one-fifth of 543.
272 is a majority of the House.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the election and tenure of the Speaker:

1. The Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members by a simple majority of those present and voting.
2. By convention the Speaker serves the whole life of the Lok Sabha even if the government changes.
3. The Constitution places no limit on re-electing a Speaker so long as he remains a member.
4. The Speaker's term ends automatically on dissolution, as the Ministers' term does.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members by a simple majority of those present and voting. Statement 2 is correct: By convention the Speaker serves the whole life of the Lok Sabha even if the government changes. Statement 3 is correct: The Constitution places no limit on re-electing a Speaker so long as he remains a member. Statement 4 is incorrect: He continues till the new House meets, unlike Ministers.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.87
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.87
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of the Speaker:

1. A resolution for his removal must be passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha.
2. At least 14 days' notice is needed before the resolution is moved.
3. While the resolution is pending, he presides but may not vote.
4. While it is pending, he may take part and vote in the first instance but has no casting vote.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.336. Statement 2 is correct: At least 14 days' notice is needed before the resolution is moved. Statement 3 is incorrect: He cannot preside, though he may speak and vote in the first instance (Laxmikanth ch23 p.336). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.336.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.88

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers of the Speaker:

1. He maintains order and decorum with the final say on discipline, and his reading of the Constitution, the Rules and precedents is final within the House.
2. He exercises a vote in the first instance as well as a casting vote on questions before the House.
3. He presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses summoned by the President to resolve a deadlock.
4. He may allow a secret sitting at the request of the Leader of the House.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: He maintains order and decorum with the final say on discipline, and his reading of the Constitution, the Rules and precedents is final within the House. Statement 2 is incorrect: He votes only to break a tie. Statement 3 is correct: He presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses summoned by the President to resolve a deadlock. Statement 4 is correct: He may allow a secret sitting at the request of the Leader of the House.

'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.87
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker's functions:

1. His decision whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final, and he certifies Money Bills before they go to the Rajya Sabha.
2. His decision on disqualification of a member under the Tenth Schedule cannot be reviewed by any court.
3. He is the ex officio chairman of the Indian Parliamentary Group and of the Conference of Presiding Officers.
4. He chairs the Public Accounts Committee of the Lok Sabha.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.337. Statement 2 is incorrect: In Kihoto Hollohan (1992) the Supreme Court held it is subject to judicial review. Statement 3 is correct: He is the ex officio chairman of the Indian Parliamentary Group and of the Conference of Presiding Officers. Statement 4 is incorrect: He chairs the Business Advisory, Rules and General Purposes Committees and appoints the chairpersons of the other committees (Laxmikanth ch23 p.337).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha:

1. He is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members by a simple majority of those present and voting.

3. He resigns by writing to the Speaker.
4. He is removable by a resolution of an effective majority with 14 days' notice, and cannot preside while it is considered.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: He is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members by a simple majority of those present and voting. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Speaker fixes it (Laxmikanth ch23 p.338). Statement 3 is correct: He resigns by writing to the Speaker. Statement 4 is correct: He is removable by a resolution of an effective majority with 14 days' notice, and cannot preside while it is considered.

2. While presiding he votes in the first instance and also has a casting vote in a tie.
3. Whenever he is appointed to a parliamentary committee he automatically becomes its chairperson.
4. The convention of offering the post to the Opposition is constitutionally binding.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: He presides when the Speaker is absent or the office is vacant and then has all the Speaker's powers. Statement 2 is incorrect: He has only a casting vote (Laxmikanth ch23 p.338). Statement 3 is correct: Whenever he is appointed to a parliamentary committee he automatically becomes its chairperson. Statement 4 is incorrect: It is only a convention (Laxmikanth ch23 p.339).
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.89
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.89
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.89

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker Pro Tem:

1. Article 95(1) lets the President appoint a Lok Sabha member to do the Speaker's duties when both the Speaker's and the Deputy Speaker's offices are vacant.
2. The situation arises right after a general election, when the new House first meets.
3. By convention the senior-most member is chosen, and the President administers the oath to him.
4. The office ceases once the House elects its permanent Speaker, so it lasts only a few days.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 95(1) lets the President appoint a Lok Sabha member to do the Speaker's duties when both the Speaker's and the Deputy Speaker's offices are vacant. Statement 2 is correct: The situation arises right after a general election, when the new House first meets. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.340. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.340.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.89

questions.q:
According to Laxmikanth, consider the following statements about the presiding officers of the Lok Sabha:

1. G.V. Mavalankar and Ananthasayanam Ayyangar were the first Speaker and the first Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
2. In the warrant of precedence the Speaker outranks every Cabinet Minister other than the Prime Minister and the Deputy Prime Minister.
3. On assuming office the Speaker takes a separate oath of office, in addition to his oath as a member.
4. The Government of India Act 1935 renamed the President and Deputy President of the central legislative assembly as Speaker and Deputy Speaker, though the old names continued till 1947.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.339. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.338. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker make no separate oath or affirmation (Laxmikanth ch23 p.339). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.339.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about vacating the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker:

1. The Speaker leaves office on ceasing to be a member of the Lok Sabha.
2. The Deputy Speaker serves for the life of the Lok Sabha unless he ceases to be a member, resigns in writing to the Speaker, or is removed.
3. The Deputy Speaker cannot preside while a resolution for his removal is under consideration.
4. The notice of a resolution to remove the Speaker must be supported by at least 100 members.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.336. Statement 2 is correct: The Deputy Speaker serves for the life of the Lok Sabha unless he ceases to be a member, resigns in writing to the Speaker, or is removed. questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:

1. If there is no quorum, he adjourns the House or suspends the meeting; the quorum is one-tenth of the total membership.
2. He summons the joint sitting of the two Houses to settle a deadlock on a Bill.
3. He votes in the first instance and may also exercise a casting vote in a tie.
4. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha shares with him the power to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: If there is no quorum, he adjourns the House or suspends the meeting; the quorum is one-tenth of the total membership. Statement 2 is incorrect: The President summons it; the Speaker presides. Statement 3 is incorrect: He votes only to break a tie. Statement 4 is incorrect: Only the Speaker decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill, and his decision is final (Laxmikanth ch23 p.359). So exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:

1. Under Article 94 the Speaker resigns by writing to the President.
2. His reading of the Constitution, the Rules of Procedure and the precedents is final within the House.
3. There is no constitutional limit on re-electing a person as Speaker, provided he remains a member.
4. He continues as Speaker for the rest of the term of the House even after he ceases to be a member of the Lok Sabha.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: He resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker. Statement 2 is correct: He is the final interpreter within the House. Statement 3 is correct: There is no constitutional limit on re-electing a person as Speaker, provided he remains a member. Statement 4 is incorrect: He leaves office on ceasing to be a member, as by disqualification (Laxmikanth ch23 p.336). So exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: statements 2 and 3 are both correct.
'Only three' miscounts: statements 1 and 4 are incorrect.
'All four' miscounts: statements 1 and 4 are incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker Pro Tem:

1. He swears in the new members and enables the House to elect its permanent Speaker.
2. By convention he takes no major procedural or political decision.
3. He is elected by the outgoing Lok Sabha before its dissolution.
4. The office continues until the end of the first session of the new House.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: He swears in the new members and enables the House to elect its permanent Speaker. Statement 2 is correct: By convention he takes no major procedural or political decision. Statement 3 is incorrect: The President appoints him. Statement 4 is incorrect: It ceases when the House elects its Speaker, a matter of a few days. So exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Speaker is the ex officio chairman of the Indian Parliamentary Group.
Statement-II: The Speaker appoints the chairpersons of the committees of the Lok Sabha and supervises their working.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: he is ex officio chairman of the Indian Parliamentary Group and the Conference of Presiding Officers (Laxmikanth ch23 p.337). Statement-II is correct: he appoints committee chairpersons and himself chairs the Business Advisory, Rules and General Purposes Committees. They are separate functions of the office, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.
w: Chairing the Parliamentary Group is a separate function; appointing committee chairpersons is not the reason for it.
Statement-II is not incorrect: the Speaker appoints committee chairpersons.
Statement-I is not incorrect: he is ex officio chairman of the Indian Parliamentary Group.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A decision of the Speaker on the disqualification of a member under the Tenth Schedule is open to judicial review.
Statement-II: In Kihoto Hollohan (1992) the Supreme Court held that the Speaker's decision on such disqualification is immune from judicial review.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Speaker's decision on Tenth Schedule disqualification can be reviewed by the courts. Statement-II is incorrect: in Kihoto Hollohan (1992) the Supreme Court held the decision subject to judicial review, so it is not immune.
w: Statement-II states the opposite of the ruling, so it cannot be correct or explain Statement-I.
Statement-II is the reverse of what the Court held, so the two cannot both be correct.
Statement-I is correct: Kihoto Hollohan made the decision reviewable.

Match the entries in List-I with the correct entries in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 93
B. Article 94
C. Article 95

1. Salaries and allowances of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker

C and D are swapped: Article 95 is the performance of duties and Article 97 is salaries.

concepts.name: Panels, the Vice-President as Chairman and the Secretariat
concepts.description: The Lok Sabha panel of chairpersons, the Vice-President's election and removal, the Speaker versus Chairman, the Deputy Chairperson and the Secretariat under Article 98.
concepts.idea: Presiding arrangements distinguish absence (panel, Deputy) from vacancy (a President-appointed member), and the Secretariat is autonomous under the presiding officer.
concepts.rule: The Speaker nominates a panel of up to ten chairpersons, who preside only in absence. The Vice-President (five years) is elected by both Houses (elected and nominated members) by STV; the Supreme Court decides disputes. He is removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution (all then members) agreed by the Lok Sabha, with 14 days' notice. Only the Speaker certifies Money Bills and presides over joint sittings; the Speaker may vote in the first instance on his own removal, the Chairman cannot. The Deputy Chairperson is removed under Article 90(c). The panel of Vice-Chairpersons is under the House rules. Article 98 gives each House a separate Secretariat headed by a permanent Secretary-General appointed by the presiding officer.
concepts.example: While the Vice-President acts as President, the Deputy Chairman performs the Chairman's duties.

questions.q: Under the Rules of the Lok Sabha a panel of chairpersons may preside over the House in the absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker. Who nominates the panel, and of how many members at most?
questions.a: The Speaker, a panel of not more than ten members
o: The Speaker, a panel of not more than ten members
The Deputy Speaker, a panel of not more than ten members
The Speaker, a panel of not more than five members
The President, a panel of not more than fifteen members
questions.e: The Speaker nominates from among the members a panel of not more than ten chairpersons (Laxmikanth ch23 p.339).
w: The Deputy Speaker has no power to nominate the panel.
The ceiling is ten, not five.
The President has no role in nominating the panel; the ceiling is ten.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the electoral college that elects the Vice-President of India?
questions.a: Elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament, without the State legislators
o: Elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament, without the State legislators
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the State Legislative Assemblies
Elected members of the Lok Sabha alone
All members of both Houses of Parliament and of the State Legislative Councils
