questions.q: All doubts and disputes concerning the election of the Vice-President of India are inquired into and decided by:
questions.a: The Supreme Court, whose decision is final
o: The Supreme Court, whose decision is final
The Election Commission of India, subject to appeal to the Supreme Court
The High Court of Delhi, subject to appeal to the Supreme Court
A joint committee of both Houses of Parliament
questions.e: The Supreme Court decides such disputes and its decision is final (Laxmikanth ch19 p.301).
w: The Commission conducts the election but does not decide disputes about it.
A High Court has no jurisdiction here.
Parliament has no committee for this purpose.

questions.q: The Secretary-General is the permanent head of the secretariat of each House of Parliament. By whom is he appointed?
questions.a: The presiding officer of that House
o: The presiding officer of that House
The President, on the advice of the Council of Ministers
The Prime Minister, as Leader of the House
questions.e: Each House has a permanent non-political Secretary-General appointed by its presiding officer (Laxmikanth ch23 p.342).
w: He is not a ministerial appointee, which would defeat the autonomy of the Secretariat.
The Prime Minister has no such role.
The UPSC does not select him.

questions.q: For the period during which the Vice-President acts as President, who performs the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
o: A member of the panel of Vice-Chairpersons
questions.e: While acting as President the Vice-President gives up the Chairman's role and the Deputy Chairman performs it, with full powers (Laxmikanth ch23 p.341).
w: The panel serves temporary absences, not this arrangement.
The Leader of the House holds no presiding authority.
The Secretary-General is an official and cannot preside.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the panel of chairpersons of the Lok Sabha:

1. It is nominated by the Speaker from among the members under the Lok Sabha rules, and consists of up to ten members.
2. It is usually named at the start of a new Lok Sabha and members continue until a new panel is nominated.
3. When the offices of both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are vacant, panel members take turns presiding.
4. A panel member presiding in the absence of both officers has the Speaker's powers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It is nominated by the Speaker from among the members under the Lok Sabha rules, and consists of up to ten members. Statement 2 is correct: It is usually named at the start of a new Lok Sabha and members continue until a new panel is nominated. Statement 3 is incorrect: In a vacancy a member appointed by the President acts (Laxmikanth ch23 p.339). Statement 4 is correct: A panel member presiding in the absence of both officers has the Speaker's powers.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.90
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.90
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the election of the Vice-President:

1. He is elected for a term of five years.
2. State legislatures take part in the electoral college.
3. The election is by proportional representation with the single transferable vote.
4. The Supreme Court decides all disputes about the election and its decision is final.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: He is elected for a term of five years. Statement 2 is incorrect: The college consists of both Houses of Parliament alone. Statement 3 is correct: The election is by proportional representation with the single transferable vote. Statement 4 is correct: The Supreme Court decides all disputes about the election and its decision is final.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.90
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.90
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Vice-President:

1. As Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha he presides, keeps order and has only a casting vote in a tie.
2. Under Article 65 he acts as President when that post is vacant or the President cannot discharge his functions.
3. While acting as President he continues to perform the Chairperson's duties as well.
4. He is removed by a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha and agreed to by the Rajya Sabha.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: As Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha he presides, keeps order and has only a casting vote in a tie. Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 65 he acts as President when that post is vacant or the President cannot discharge his functions. Statement 3 is incorrect: He gives up the Chairperson's role and the Deputy Chairperson performs it. Statement 4 is incorrect: The resolution is passed by the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.90
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of the Vice-President:

1. The resolution is passed by a majority of all then members of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha by a simple majority.
2. It must originate in the Rajya Sabha and needs 14 days' notice.
3. The Constitution lists no grounds for his removal.
4. He cannot vote on the resolution, though he may be present and take part in the proceedings.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch19 p.304. Statement 2 is correct: It must originate in the Rajya Sabha and needs 14 days' notice. Statement 3 is correct: The Constitution lists no grounds for his removal. Statement 4 is correct: Article 92; Laxmikanth ch23 p.340.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.90
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.90
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha:

1. Only the Speaker decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
2. Both the Speaker and the Chairperson preside over a joint sitting of the two Houses.
3. The Speaker is a member of the Lok Sabha, while the Chairperson is not a member of the Rajya Sabha.
4. In a removal motion neither of them may vote.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Only the Speaker decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill. Statement 2 is incorrect: Only the Speaker does; the Deputy Speaker if he is absent (Laxmikanth ch23 p.338). Statement 3 is correct: The Speaker is a member of the Lok Sabha, while the Chairperson is not a member of the Rajya Sabha. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Speaker may vote in the first instance; the Chairperson cannot vote.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.90
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairperson:

1. Neither votes in the first instance, and each has only a casting vote in a tie.
2. The Speaker's salary is subject to the annual vote of Parliament, whereas the Chairperson's is charged on the Consolidated Fund.
3. Both are barred from presiding while a resolution for their removal is under consideration.
4. The salary of the Deputy Chairperson is fixed by Parliament by law under Article 97 and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Neither votes in the first instance, and each has only a casting vote in a tie. Statement 2 is incorrect: Both are charged on the Consolidated Fund and are not voted. Statement 3 is correct: Both are barred from presiding while a resolution for their removal is under consideration. Statement 4 is correct: The salary of the Deputy Chairperson is fixed by Parliament by law under Article 97 and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.91
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha:

1. Article 89 provides for him, and the Rajya Sabha elects him from among its members.
2. When the post falls vacant the House elects a replacement at the earliest.
3. His removal by resolution is provided for in Article 92.
4. He is not subordinate to the Chairperson but answerable directly to the Rajya Sabha.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 89 provides for him, and the Rajya Sabha elects him from among its members. Statement 2 is correct: When the post falls vacant the House elects a replacement at the earliest. Statement 3 is incorrect: Removal is under Article 90(c); Article 92 only bars him from presiding during the resolution. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.341.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.91
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha:

1. He takes over the Chairperson's functions when that office is vacant or the Vice-President discharges the President's duties, with full powers while presiding.
2. While presiding, he has a vote in the first instance as well as a casting vote.
3. The Constitution itself provides, in Article 91, a panel of Vice-Chairpersons to preside when the Chairperson and Deputy Chairperson are absent.
4. His salary and allowances are fixed by Parliament by law under Article 97 and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: He takes over the Chairperson's functions when that office is vacant or the Vice-President discharges the President's duties, with full powers while presiding. Statement 2 is incorrect: He has only a casting vote (Laxmikanth ch23 p.341). Statement 3 is incorrect: The panel exists under the Rajya Sabha Rules; Article 91 only lets the House decide who presides (Laxmikanth ch23 p.341). Statement 4 is correct: His salary and allowances are fixed by Parliament by law under Article 97 and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.91
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.91
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Secretariats of Parliament:

1. Article 98 provides for a separate Secretariat for each House.
2. The arrangement protects the legislature's autonomy from executive interference, staff recruitment and service conditions being regulated by Parliament.
3. Each Secretariat works under the guidance of the Council of Ministers.
4. The Secretary-General is appointed by the President and changes with the government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 98 provides for a separate Secretariat for each House. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.342. Statement 3 is incorrect: It works under the guidance and control of the presiding officer. Statement 4 is incorrect: He is a permanent non-political officer appointed by the presiding officer.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.92
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about presiding over the Rajya Sabha:

1. The Constitution distinguishes absence of a presiding officer from vacancy of the office.
2. When both the Chairperson and Deputy Chairperson offices are vacant, a member appointed by the President performs the Chairperson's functions.
3. In a vacancy of both offices, members of the panel of Vice-Chairpersons may preside.
4. If no panel member is available, the Chairman picks any member to preside.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Constitution distinguishes absence of a presiding officer from vacancy of the office. Statement 2 is correct: When both the Chairperson and Deputy Chairperson offices are vacant, a member appointed by the President performs the Chairperson's functions. Statement 3 is incorrect: The panel works only in temporary absences (Laxmikanth ch23 p.341). Statement 4 is incorrect: The House itself decides which member presides. So exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Secretary-General of a House of Parliament:

1. He is the chief procedural adviser to the presiding officer and adviser to members on practice, procedure and precedents.
2. He acts as secretary to all the parliamentary committees of the House.
3. The Secretariat functions under the guidance and control of the presiding officer, not the Council of Ministers.
4. He is a political appointee who changes with the government.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: He is the chief procedural adviser to the presiding officer and adviser to members on practice, procedure and precedents. Statement 2 is correct: He acts as secretary to all the parliamentary committees of the House. Statement 3 is correct: The Secretariat functions under the guidance and control of the presiding officer, not the Council of Ministers. Statement 4 is incorrect: He is a permanent non-political officer. So exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Vice-President and the Deputy Chairperson:

1. Under Article 65 the Vice-President acts as President when the post is vacant or the President cannot discharge his functions.
2. The Vice-President is elected for a term of six years.
3. The Deputy Chairperson resigns by writing to the President.
4. The Deputy Chairperson is subordinate to the Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 65 the Vice-President acts as President when the post is vacant or the President cannot discharge his functions. Statement 2 is incorrect: The term is five years. Statement 3 is incorrect: He resigns by writing to the Chairperson. Statement 4 is incorrect: He is answerable directly to the Rajya Sabha. So exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: While the Vice-President acts as President, he does not perform the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Statement-II: While so acting, the Vice-President continues to draw the salary of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: (Laxmikanth ch23 p.340). Statement-II is incorrect: during this period he is paid the salary and allowances of the President, and is not entitled to the Chairman's (Laxmikanth ch23 p.340).
w: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Statement-II is incorrect, so the pair is not both correct.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The salary of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is not voted upon annually by Parliament.
Statement-II: The salary of the Speaker is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: and. Statement-II is correct: the salaries of the presiding officers are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not voted on annually. A charged expenditure is only discussed, not put to the annual vote, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
w: Being charged on the Consolidated Fund is exactly why the salary is not put to the annual vote, so II does explain I.
Statement-II is not incorrect: the salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund.
Statement-I is not incorrect: the Speaker's salary is not subject to the annual vote.

questions.q:
Match the entries in List-I with the correct entries in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 89
B. Article 90
C. Article 91
D. Article 92

List-II
1. The Chairman or Deputy Chairman not to preside while a resolution for removal is under consideration
2. Vacation of, resignation from and removal from the office of Deputy Chairman
3. Power of the Deputy Chairman or other person to perform the duties of the Chairman
4. The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States
questions.e: Article 89 provides for the Chairman and Deputy Chairman; Article 90 for vacation, resignation and removal of the Deputy Chairman; Article 91 for performance of the Chairman's duties by the Deputy Chairman or another person; Article 92 for the bar on presiding during a removal resolution.
w: A and B are swapped: Article 89 is about the offices and Article 90 about the Deputy Chairman's vacation and removal.
C and D are swapped: Article 91 is performance of duties and Article 92 is the bar on presiding.
B and C are swapped: Article 90 is removal and Article 91 is performance of duties.

concepts.name: Leaders, whips and the budget in Parliament
concepts.description: Leader of the House, Leader of the Opposition, whips and the constitutional provisions on the budget and the role of the two Houses.
concepts.idea: The Leader of the House and the Leader of the Opposition are recognised by Rules and by the 1977 Act, whips by convention, and the budget by Articles 112-119.
concepts.rule: The Leader of the House is the Prime Minister (or a Minister nominated by him) in the Lok Sabha, and a Minister from the Rajya Sabha there; the post is under the Rules. The Leader of the Opposition gained official recognition in 1969, statutory status in 1977, Cabinet-minister rank, and sits on selection committees for the CBI Director, CVC, CIC, Lokpal and NHRC. Whips rest on convention. Article 112 requires the Annual Financial Statement; Art 113 demands on the President's recommendation; Art 114 appropriation by law; Art 116 Vote on Account; Art 265 tax by authority of law. The Rajya Sabha cannot vote on demands and must return a Money Bill within 14 days. The Budget is presented on 1 February since 2017, with no discussion that day.
concepts.example: The Rajya Sabha can discuss the Budget but cannot vote on demands for grants; the Lok Sabha cannot increase a demand.

questions.q: The Leader of the Opposition in each House of Parliament was given statutory recognition in which year, and under which Act?
questions.a: 1977, under the Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act
o: 1977, under the Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act
1969, under the Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act
1998, under the Leaders and Chief Whips of Recognised Parties and Groups in Parliament (Facilities) Act
1952, under the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The 1977 Act gave statutory recognition; 1969 is when an official Leader of the Opposition was first recognised, by convention (Laxmikanth ch23 p.342).
w: 1969 is the year of first recognition, which was by convention and not by any Act.
The 1998 Act gives telephone and secretarial facilities to leaders and Chief Whips of recognised parties; it did not confer the statutory status.
The Rules of Procedure do not give the Leader of the Opposition statutory status.

questions.q: The office of whip in Parliament has which one of the following bases?
questions.a: It rests on parliamentary convention and is in neither the Constitution nor the Rules of the House
o: It rests on parliamentary convention and is in neither the Constitution nor the Rules of the House
It is created by the Tenth Schedule, which also lists the duties of a whip in the House
It is provided in the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, which list its duties
It is created by Article 105, which protects the freedom of speech of members of Parliament
questions.e: The office of whip is based on convention; it is mentioned in neither the Constitution nor the Rules of the House (Laxmikanth ch23 p.343).
w: The Tenth Schedule speaks of directions issued by the political party but does not create the office of whip.
The Rules of the House do not mention the office.
Article 105 deals with powers, privileges and immunities of members and does not create the office.

questions.q: The Government wishes to spend money from the Consolidated Fund of India although no law has authorised the expenditure. Which Article bars the withdrawal?
questions.e: Article 114 requires an appropriation law for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund (Laxmikanth ch23 p.364).
w: Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement.
Article 113 provides for the procedure for demands for grants.
Article 265 provides that no tax may be levied or collected except by authority of law.

questions.q: A Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, which keeps it for more than 14 days without returning it. What is the position?
questions.a: The Bill is deemed passed by both Houses in the form the Lok Sabha passed it
o: The Bill is deemed passed by both Houses in the form the Lok Sabha passed it
The Bill lapses and has to be reintroduced afresh in the Lok Sabha by the Minister
The President summons a joint sitting of both Houses to resolve the deadlock
The Bill is deemed passed with all the amendments the Rajya Sabha would have recommended
questions.e: If the Rajya Sabha does not return the Bill within 14 days it is deemed passed in the form passed by the Lok Sabha (Laxmikanth ch23 p.359).
w: Nothing lapses; the deemed-passage rule applies.
A joint sitting is for ordinary Bills; a Money Bill has the special 14-day rule.
The Rajya Sabha can only recommend amendments, and none are deemed accepted.

questions.q: Since 2017 the Union Budget has been presented to Parliament on which date, and what was the practice before that?
questions.a: 1 February; earlier on the last working day of February
o: 1 February; earlier on the last working day of February
28 February; earlier on 31 March, the close of the financial year
1 March; earlier on the first working day of April, the start of the year
31 January; earlier on 15 February, the date of the Economic Survey
questions.e: Since 2017 the Budget is presented on 1 February, a month earlier than the earlier convention of the last working day of February (Laxmikanth ch23 p.366).
w: 28 February and 31 March are not the dates in either period.
1 March was not the date, and April 1 begins the financial year.
31 January is the day the Budget session begins, with the Economic Survey, not the date of the Budget.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Leader of the House:

1. In the Lok Sabha the Prime Minister, as leader of the majority party, is the Leader of the House.
2. In the Rajya Sabha a Minister who is a member of that House is nominated to the post.
3. The post is recognised under the Rules of Procedure of each House and is not a constitutional office.
4. The Leader of the House is the main liaison between the presiding officer and the Council of Ministers on the dates for summoning, adjournment and prorogation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: In the Lok Sabha the Prime Minister, as leader of the majority party, is the Leader of the House. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.342. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.343. Statement 4 is correct: The Leader of the House is the main liaison between the presiding officer and the Council of Ministers on the dates for summoning, adjournment and prorogation.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.92
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Leader of the Opposition:

1. The office was created by the Constitution in 1950.
2. The recognition of an official Leader of the Opposition in 1969 came eight years before his statutory status.
3. He is entitled to the salary, allowances and rank of a Cabinet Minister.
4. He is the leader of the largest party not in government, recognised by the Speaker or Chairman; a party needs at least one-tenth of the House to be recognised.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It began on convention; an official Leader was first recognised in 1969 and the office was given statutory status in 1977. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.342. Statement 3 is correct: He is entitled to the salary, allowances and rank of a Cabinet Minister. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.342; the one-tenth rests on the directions of the Speaker and Chairman.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.92
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Leader of the Opposition and appointments to statutory bodies:

1. He sits on the selection committee for the Chief Vigilance Commissioner.
2. He sits on the selection committee for Central Information Commissioners.
3. He sits on the selection committee for the Lokpal.
4. He sits on a selection committee for the Comptroller and Auditor General.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: He sits on the selection committee for the Chief Vigilance Commissioner. Statement 2 is correct: He sits on the selection committee for Central Information Commissioners. Statement 3 is correct: He sits on the selection committee for the Lokpal. Statement 4 is incorrect: The CAG is appointed by the President; no such committee exists.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about whips in Parliament:

1. The office of whip is provided in the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha.
2. Each major party appoints a Chief Whip, assisted by additional whips chosen from among MPs.
3. A two-line whip directs members how to vote on the question put to the House.
4. The Chief Whip supplies the party's list of speakers to the Speaker or the Chairman.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It is mentioned neither in the Constitution nor in the Rules (Laxmikanth ch23 p.343). Statement 2 is correct: Each major party appoints a Chief Whip, assisted by additional whips chosen from among MPs. Statement 3 is incorrect: A two-line whip only directs members to be present during the voting, without telling them how to vote. Statement 4 is correct: The Chief Whip supplies the party's list of speakers to the Speaker or the Chairman.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.93
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.93
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.93

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about whips:

1. The Chief Whip ensures attendance at important votes and directs members to vote according to the whip issued.
2. The Chief Whip informs members of the party's official stand on Bills and motions.
3. A three-line whip is the mildest form, merely informing members of an upcoming vote.
4. A one-line whip compels members to vote as directed.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.343. Statement 2 is correct: The Chief Whip informs members of the party's official stand on Bills and motions. Statement 3 is incorrect: It is the strongest, directing members to vote strictly on the party line. Statement 4 is incorrect: A one-line whip only informs members of a vote; they may abstain (by common usage).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.93
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.93
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.93

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional provisions on the budget:

1. Article 119 empowers Parliament to regulate by law the procedure in Parliament for timely completion of financial business.
2. A demand for a grant may be made on the Finance Minister's own recommendation.
3. Under Article 112 the President causes the Annual Financial Statement to be laid before both Houses for every financial year.
4. The Annual Financial Statement shows separately the expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund and distinguishes revenue-account expenditure from other expenditure.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 119 empowers Parliament to regulate by law the procedure in Parliament for timely completion of financial business. Statement 2 is incorrect: The recommendation must be the President's (Article 113). Statement 3 is correct: Under Article 112 the President causes the Annual Financial Statement to be laid before both Houses for every financial year. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.364-365.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.93
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.93
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.93

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the role of the two Houses in the budget:

1. A Money Bill dealing with taxation can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and on the President's recommendation.
2. According to Laxmikanth, a Money Bill or Finance Bill dealing with taxation cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
3. Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund is put to the vote of the Lok Sabha, though it can also be discussed.
4. The Lok Sabha may approve, refuse or reduce a demand for grant, and may also increase it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.359. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.364. Statement 3 is incorrect: It is not subject to voting; it can only be discussed. Statement 4 is incorrect: It cannot increase it.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.93
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.93
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.93

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passing of money measures:

1. No tax may be levied or collected except by authority of law, under Article 265.
2. No amendment may be proposed to the Appropriation Bill that changes the amount of any voted grant or of charged expenditure.
3. A Vote on Account is authorised by the Rajya Sabha when the Budget process runs beyond the financial year.
4. The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days, with or without recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: No tax may be levied or collected except by authority of law, under Article 265. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch23 p.368. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Lok Sabha authorises it (Article 116). Statement 4 is correct: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days, with or without recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.93
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.93
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.93

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Union Budget:

1. The Finance Minister presents the Budget with a Budget Speech in the Lok Sabha covering the state of the economy, fiscal priorities and key tax and expenditure proposals.
2. The Constitution does not require the Budget to be in a single document; it may be presented in two or more parts, each treated as a complete budget.
3. A general debate on the Budget takes place on the day it is presented.
4. After the Finance Minister's speech in the Lok Sabha the Budget is laid before the Rajya Sabha, which can discuss it but cannot vote on demands for grants.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Finance Minister presents the Budget with a Budget Speech in the Lok Sabha covering the state of the economy, fiscal priorities and key tax and expenditure proposals. Statement 2 is correct: The Constitution does not require the Budget to be in a single document; it may be presented in two or more parts, each treated as a complete budget. Statement 3 is incorrect: No discussion takes place that day (Laxmikanth ch23 p.366). Statement 4 is correct: After the Finance Minister's speech in the Lok Sabha the Budget is laid before the Rajya Sabha, which can discuss it but cannot vote on demands for grants.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.94
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.94
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.94

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. In the Rajya Sabha the Leader of the House is a senior Cabinet Minister who belongs to that House.
2. In the Rajya Sabha the Prime Minister is the Leader of the House even when he is a member of the Lok Sabha.
3. The Leader of the Opposition sits on the selection committee for the Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation.
4. A party is recognised for the post of Leader of the Opposition only if it has at least one-fourth of the strength of the House.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: In the Rajya Sabha the Leader of the House is a senior Cabinet Minister who belongs to that House. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Prime Minister leads the House only in the Lok Sabha; in the Rajya Sabha a Cabinet Minister who is a member of it is nominated (Laxmikanth ch23 p.342). Statement 3 is correct: The Leader of the Opposition sits on the selection committee for the Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation. Statement 4 is incorrect: The party needs at least one-tenth of the House (Laxmikanth ch23 p.342). So exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Leader of the House prepares and steers government business, including the scheduling of motions and debates.
2. After presentation in the Lok Sabha the Budget is laid before the Rajya Sabha, which may discuss it.
3. Article 119 empowers the President, by an ordinance, to regulate the procedure in Parliament for the timely completion of financial business.
4. For every financial year the President causes the Annual Financial Statement to be laid before both Houses.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Leader of the House prepares and steers government business, including the scheduling of motions and debates. Statement 2 is correct: After presentation in the Lok Sabha the Budget is laid before the Rajya Sabha, which may discuss it. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 119 empowers Parliament to regulate that procedure by law, not the President by ordinance. Statement 4 is correct: Article 112. So exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: statements 1, 2 and 4 are all correct.
'Only one' miscounts: statements 1, 2 and 4 are all correct.
'All four' miscounts: statement 3 is incorrect, since Article 119 speaks of a law of Parliament.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Rajya Sabha may vote on demands for grants as well as the Lok Sabha.
2. The Budget is first presented in the Rajya Sabha and then laid before the Lok Sabha.
3. An amendment to the Appropriation Bill may vary the amount of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund.
4. The Budget may be presented in two or more parts, each treated as a complete budget.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Voting on demands for grants is the exclusive privilege of the Lok Sabha. Statement 2 is incorrect: It is presented in the Lok Sabha and then laid before the Rajya Sabha. Statement 3 is incorrect: No such amendment may be proposed. Statement 4 is correct: . So exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Union Budget has been presented on 1 February since 2017.
Statement-II: The earlier date was advanced so that Parliament could pass the Appropriation Bill before the end of the financial year, avoiding a Vote on Account.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: (Laxmikanth ch23 p.366). Statement-II is correct: (Laxmikanth ch23 p.369) and explains it: the advancement is meant to let Parliament pass a single Appropriation Bill before the financial year closes.
w: Statement-II gives the purpose of the advancement, so it explains Statement-I.
Statement-II is not incorrect; the aim was to avoid a Vote on Account.
Statement-I is not incorrect; the Budget is presented on 1 February.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Lok Sabha may approve, refuse or reduce a demand for grant, but it cannot increase it.
Statement-II: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is open to discussion but not to voting in the Lok Sabha.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: The Lok Sabha may approve, refuse or reduce a demand for grant, but it cannot increase it. Statement-II is correct: charged expenditure may be discussed but is not voted. The limit on increasing a demand for grant is about the voted demands and has nothing to do with charged expenditure being non-votable, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.
w: Charged expenditure is outside the vote altogether, whereas the power to reduce or refuse concerns voted demands; II is not the reason.
Statement-II is not incorrect: charged expenditure is discussed but not voted.
Statement-I is not incorrect: the House can reduce or refuse a demand but not increase it.

questions.q:
Match the entries in List-I with the correct entries in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 112
B. Article 113
C. Article 114
D. Article 116

List-II
1. Vote on Account
2. Annual Financial Statement
3. Demands for grants on the President's recommendation
4. Appropriation by law for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund
questions.e: Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement; Article 113 for demands for grants on the President's recommendation; Article 114 for appropriation by law; Article 116 for the Vote on Account (Laxmikanth ch23 p.365).
w: A and B are swapped: Article 112 is the Annual Financial Statement and Article 113 is demands for grants.
C and D are swapped: Article 114 is appropriation and Article 116 is Vote on Account.
B and C are swapped: Article 113 is demands for grants and Article 114 is appropriation.
